thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: High CPU usage + OOMs in serving-prod (tokenizer): multiple pods killed in us-west-2. Pager: @oncall (priority: P1) :rotating_light:

mike: Seeing ~30% of tokenizer preproc pods OOMing in the last 5m. Pod restarts and some node flaps. Service-level errors: 5xxs up from 0.3% -> 7% for /v1/generate.

sophie: Thanks — working to triage. Any obvious recent deploy?

mike: No deploys in the last 6 hours. Load history shows a sudden burst of very long prompts hitting preproc, CPU jumps and kernel OOM logs on nodes.

jordan: Can you paste the kubectl describe + logs from one of the killed pods?

mike: Pasting truncated logs:

```
Killed process 12456 (tokenizer) total-vm: 2147483648kB, anon-rss: 1960000kB
kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 12456 (tokenizer)
RuntimeError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered (in a different set of pods we also saw GPU faults)
```

mike: Also seeing node kernel message: "memory cgroup out of memory: kill process 12456 (tokenizer)" on 3 nodes.

maya: I'm seeing correlated autoscaler activity — pods got scheduled to nodes with low headroom. Could be poor scheduling + a spike in per-request CPU due to long prompts and heavy pre-tokenization.

infra-bot: DETECTED: node-usw2a experienced kernel panic 2026-11-05T03:12:04Z; cordon recommended.

sophie: Ok immediate mitigation plan: 1) Evict tokenizer preproc pods from suspect nodes via pod disruption; 2) Temporarily increase replica count on dedicated preproc pool with CPU-limits to spread load; 3) Apply admission control to reject/queue oversized prompts.

mike: Running a safe rollout: `kubectl cordon node/usw2a-03 && kubectl drain node/usw2a-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`

jordan: Creating a temporary mutating webhook rule to limit prompt length to 20000 chars for the next 30m, and a rate-limiter at the ingress. Patch applied: `kubectl apply -f patch-limit-prompt.yaml`

mike: Scaling preproc-deployment from 10 -> 25 with CPU requests set to 800m (was 200m) to avoid bursting OOM. Command:`kubectl scale deployment preproc-deployment --replicas=25` and `kubectl set resources deployment preproc-deployment -c tokenizer --requests=800m --limits=1600m`

maya: Also enabling prefix cache for repeated long prompts on the gateway to reduce preproc cycles: flipping flag `GATEWAY_ENABLE_PREFIX_CACHE=true` in the configmap and rolling gateway.

customer-success: Observed customer impact: a handful of sessions returned 502s, mostly for large-batch generation jobs. Notified two enterprise customers with temporary mitigation notes.

sophie: Good. Any signs of persistent CUDA errors vs CPU OOM? Mike, you saw a CUDA device-side assert once — likely a downstream effect of memory corruption when the process was starved.

mike: Agree — primary cause looks like CPU OOM in tokenizer preproc; some pods also logged GPU faults during restart (racey).

jordan: I've added an emergency admission rule to reject prompts with > 100k tokens and to return 413 with guidance. 

mike: After scaling and cordon, restart rate dropped to normal. CPU on preproc pool stabilized from 95% -> 45% over 6m. No new OOMs in last 8m.

infra-bot: NOTE: cordon persists on nodes: [usw2a-03, usw2b-01]. Suggested next step: reprovision or run kernel upgrade on usw2a-03.

maya: Repro note for postmortem: workload had a mix of tiny concurrent requests and a small subset of extremely long prompts submitted by an internal test harness; the test harness bypassed client-side length checks. We'll add server-side prompts quotas and tighten e2e test gating.

sophie: On-call handoff: @jordan taking lead for the next 4 hours to monitor. I'll write incident page and coordinate postmortem.

jordan: Acknowledged. Monitoring alerts lowered but keeping paging level at P1 until 2hr stable window.

customer-success: Logged impacted customers and scheduled proactive outreach. No billing anomalies detected so far.

mike: Will collect `dmesg`, `kubectl describe` outputs and upload to the incident doc (links to S3). Also saving the tokenizer heap dump from one survivor pod for analysis.

sophie: TL;DR root cause hypothesis: tokenizer preproc saw extreme prompt-length spike -> uncontrolled CPU and memory growth -> kernel OOM killed processes -> some restarts hit CUDA faults while recovering. Primary mitigations: cordon flaky nodes, scale preproc with higher requests, temp admission limits + prompt-length reject, enable prefix cache. Followups: postmortem to include safer defaults, admission rules, and test harness fixes.

jordan: Handoff note: I'll check again in 30m and escalate if OOMs reappear.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: acknowledged, status -> monitoring.

mike: thanks team :heart:
